To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The incongruity-resolution model is a good starting point to analyse humorous cartoons.
the incongruity-resolution theory and the relevance theory are complementary, while the conceptual blending theory is an overarching framework.

(a) the incongruous blends are more humorous than the non incongruous blends; (b) the blends that are relevant are more humorous than those that are not relevant; (c) the blends that include a high number of elements are more humorous than blends with a lower number of elements; and (d) the blends with a high number of cognitive effects are more humorous than less cognitive effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new perspective on the analysis of humorous political cartoons and, more generally, with the application of the blending approach to humour research.
the analysis of the cognitive processes that underlie humorous blends.
a theoretical model for humour, which integrates blending, relevance theory and incongruity resolution theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incongruity theory of humour is a necessary condition for the appreciation of humour in the cartoons, whereas blending is a sufficient condition.
incongruity resolution is not a sufficient condition for humour.
incongruity, blending and relevance theory can be integrated to provide a coherent account of humorous political cartoons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incongruity and relevance theories are the most appropriate to account for the humorous effect in cartoons.
the blending model is a powerful tool to explain the cognitive mechanisms of humour appreciation.
humour is a result of a blend that is incongruous and relevant at the same time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
incongruity resolution is not an all encompassing model of humour, but rather a special case of the more general blending model, which is in turn a special case of relevance theory.
the blending approach to humour is a promising and flexible tool for analysing multimodal humorous cartoons.
the incongruity model of humour is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for the appreciation of a humorous text.
